title: First conditional
note: If/when + present, will + base. Real future. Light zero. Gap on will/won't or present verb. · Bank 48 items · flags: 2026-07-26f vocab+accepts · sequencing rewrite 2026-08-06 (cloud): 29/48 items re-lexified onto pool-legal words; 'rain' kept as the single logged fork · intro rewritten student-facing 2026-08-16 (was authoring shorthand — James, smoking for Patrik) · gap-half rewrite 2026-08-19 (James, Patrik smoke): 17 blanks moved onto the if/time clause — the bank only ever tested the result half; + 6 as soon as/until/after items the intro promised · 2026-08-20 (James, smoke): "this is zero conditional and it is labelled first conditional — sloppy, embarrassing". Intro card 5 taught present+present facts under a First conditional heading with nothing naming it; 6 of the 54 items are the same shape. The card now names the zero conditional and states the contrast, and those 6 items explain themselves as zero conditional when marked. The unit stays First conditional — the zero one appears only as the labelled contrast. · 2026-08-20 (James, smoke): "confusing sentence: using live as an adjective here at a2". live-as-adjective is taught nowhere at A1/A2, so an untaught word carried the meaning and any A2 student reads it as the verb. Now online (taught in a1_tech), which keeps the launch sense the Czech had. · intro card 0 rewritten 2026-08-24 (James, Patrik smoke): the Czech-marks-it-twice insight was buried as a bullet on the 'Examples' card, arriving after the rule; promoted to card 0 and reframed as 'one future per sentence — the if-half borrows it', so the card kills the transfer error instead of restating the form. 13 of Patrik's 42 logged errors sit on this unit. · card 0 given an orientation opening 2026-08-24 (James, smoking for the link check): the rewrite earlier that day led with the Czech contrast and had dropped the sentence saying what a conditional IS, so a student met the correction before the concept. Orientation first, then the contrast — the b1_articles_advanced card-0 pattern. · 2026-08-24 (James, smoke flag): the walk-home item was an always-true item whose CZECH PROMPT was future (přijdeš = you will arrive), so the honest translation 'you'll be late' was marked wrong — his flag, and a credibility problem. James chose to change the English rather than the Czech (he does not read Czech, so do not ask him to validate Czech wording). Now an ordinary first-conditional item: en/gap/gap_answer/accepts/explanation/quiz_options all moved together. Always-true items in this unit: 6 -> 5. · 2026-08-24 (same pass): the four remaining always-true items carried no signal that they wanted no `will`, so the student had no way to tell them from the first-conditional items around them — (vždy platí) added to each, matching the ice-melting item which already used it. Also accepted 'you are tired' on the don't-eat item: its Czech says jsi (are), so that is the faithful translation and it was being marked wrong. · lenient_if_when 2026-08-24: Czech kdyz is both if and when, and this pack teaches that when/until/as soon as/after behave like if — so it accepted only If and marked When wrong, contradicting its own card. Opt-in flag; unreal-conditional packs must NOT set it. · card 0 connector points revised 2026-08-24 (James): 'behave exactly like if' was a TENSE claim being read as a meaning claim — they take the same present simple but if is uncertain and when is expected. With lenient_if_when now accepting both, silent forgiveness would teach nothing, so the card states the leniency and the difference. Cards 1 and 5 keep the old phrasing deliberately: they are in a tense context.

cards.title: What is a conditional?
points: Two halves: the **if**-half, and the result
First conditional = a real future possibility
Czech marks the future twice
English marks it once: **will** only in the result
The if-half stays present
Never: ~~If it **will** rain~~
**when · until · as soon as · after** take the same present as **if**
Czech **když** is if or when — both accepted here
**if** = maybe · **when** = it happens

cards.title: Examples

table.caption: English ↔ Czech
rows: Když se budeš učit, uděláš to.

points: when / until / as soon as: same present as if

cards.title: Negatives

table.caption: examples
rows: If it **doesn't** rain, we **will** go out.
If you **don't** hurry, you **will** miss the train.

points: **won't** = **will not**.
Negative in the if-part: don't / doesn't. Negative result: won't.

cards.title: Questions

table.caption: examples
rows: If you **miss** the bus, how **will** you get home?

points: **will** + person in the question half: What **will** you do…?
In the question, will moves before the person. The if-part does not change.

cards.title: Zero conditional — facts (a different one)

table.caption: facts
rows: If you **don't** water plants, they die.

points: Zero conditional (always true): If you heat ice, it **melts**.
First conditional (one future possibility): If it **rains**, I **will** stay home.
The difference is **will** — a fact never has it.
Nultý = vždy platí. První = jedna budoucí možnost. Rozdíl je **will**.
This is NOT the first conditional.
It has its own name: the **zero conditional**.
Use it when something is ALWAYS true — a fact, not a future plan.
Both halves use the present, and there is no **will** anywhere.

rows: when / until / as soon as work like if
